steps.title: The verb be: affirmative, negative and questions

explanation.en: The verb be means both 'ser' and 'estar'. English always needs a subject: say 'It is cold', never 'Is cold'. In conversation we use short forms: I'm, you're, she's. Negatives add not: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't. Questions swap the order: Are you a student? Short answers: 'Yes, I am.' / 'No, I'm not.' — never 'Yes, I'm.'
explanation.es: El verbo be significa «ser» y «estar». El inglés siempre necesita sujeto: «It is cold», nunca «Is cold». En conversación se usan formas cortas: I'm, you're, she's. La negación añade not: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't. Las preguntas invierten el orden: Are you a student? Respuestas cortas: «Yes, I am.» / «No, I'm not.»; nunca «Yes, I'm.»

watchOut.en: Don't drop the subject: 'Is a good teacher' ✗ → 'She is a good teacher' ✓. And for professions use a/an: 'I'm a nurse', not 'I'm nurse'.
watchOut.es: No omitas el sujeto: «Is a good teacher» ✗ → «She is a good teacher» ✓. Y con profesiones usa a/an: «I'm a nurse», no «I'm nurse».

exercises.prompt: Make it negative: I ___ tired. (am + not)

explanation.en: Short answers don't use contractions: Yes, I am.
explanation.es: Las respuestas cortas no usan contracción: Yes, I am.

steps.title: Short forms and the /ð/ in they

tip.en: In natural speech 'I am' becomes I'm — one syllable. For /ð/ (they, the, this) put the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth and use your voice: it vibrates. It's softer than the Spanish 'd' in 'dedo'.
tip.es: En el habla natural «I am» se vuelve I'm: una sola sílaba. Para /ð/ (they, the, this) pon la punta de la lengua entre los dientes y usa la voz: vibra. Es más suave que la «d» de «dedo».

steps.title: Describe yourself and people you know

repeat.text: Are you tired? No, I'm not.

challenge.prompt: Describe yourself and two people you know with the verb be: who they are, job or studies, and how they are today. Include one negative sentence.
challenge.promptEs: Descríbete a ti y a dos personas que conozcas con el verbo be: quiénes son, trabajo o estudios y cómo están hoy. Incluye una frase negativa.
prepare: This is my friend … He's / She's a …
challenge.model: I'm Laura. I'm a student. I'm not tired today, I'm happy! This is my friend Diego. He's a teacher. He isn't married. My parents are in Bogotá. They're fine.

label.en: I described myself and two other people, with one negative sentence.
label.es: Me describí y describí a dos personas, con una frase negativa.

label.en: Every sentence had a subject + be (I'm, he's, they're).
label.es: Cada frase tenía sujeto + be (I'm, he's, they're).

label.en: Short forms sounded like one syllable (I'm, they're).
label.es: Las formas cortas sonaron como una sílaba (I'm, they're).

label.en: I kept going without long pauses.

steps.title: Meet the Tuesday group
steps.text:
Meet the Tuesday group!

Paula is a nurse. She's 29 and she's from Cali. She isn't married.

Tom and Jessica are from Canada. They're students. They're married!

Mr. Kim is our teacher. He's from Seoul, but he's in Bogotá now. He's very patient.

explanation.en: 'He's from Seoul, but he's in Bogotá now.'
explanation.es: «Es de Seúl, pero ahora está en Bogotá».

steps.title: Me and a friend
steps.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences about you and a friend using the verb be: name, where you are from, job or studies, and how you are today. Include one negative sentence.
steps.promptEs: Escribe 4–6 frases sobre ti y un amigo/a con el verbo be: nombre, de dónde son, trabajo o estudios y cómo están hoy. Incluye una frase negativa.

label.en: A sentence about you (I'm / I am)
label.es: Una frase sobre ti (I'm / I am)

label.en: A sentence about another person (he's / she's)
label.es: Una frase sobre otra persona (he's / she's)

label.en: No sentences without a subject ('Is a…')

hint.en: Add he / she / it before is.
hint.es: Añade he / she / it antes de is.

label.en: The pronoun I is a capital letter
label.es: El pronombre I va en mayúscula
